# Adjudication Task — Chapter 644

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃644화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|띠링. 띠링. 띠링.
  6|
  7|
  8|
  9|- 퀘스트, [부족 대회의]가 생성되었습니다!
 10|
 11|퀘스트
 12|
 13|
 14|
 15|[부족 대회의]
 16|
 17|
 18|
 19|당신은 남만야수궁 역사 최초로 부족 대회의에 참석할 자격을 얻은 외지인이 되었습니다.
 20|
 21|이는 과거 열화문의 오 대 문주조차 이루지 못했던 업적입니다.
 22|
 23|왜냐하면 그는 대회의가 열리기도 전에 오독문을 멸문시키고 떠났거든요!
 24|
 25|남만의 대소사가 결정되는 이 중대한 회의에서, 당신은 지금 할 수 있는 최선의 결과를 도출해 내야 합니다!
 26|
 27|
 28|
 29|등급 : 초절정
 30|
 31|제한 : 진태경
 32|
 33|임무 : 남만야수궁의 입맹(入盟) (미완료)
 34|
 35|보상 : ???
 36|
 37|실패 : ???
 38|
 39|
 40|
 41|
 42|
 43|나는 퀘스트 창을 바라보며 내심 한숨을 내쉬었다.
 44|
 45|제아무리 나를 향한 여론이 호의적으로 변했다고는 하지만 남만야수궁을 입맹시키라니. 초절정이라는 퀘스트 등급만큼이나 빡센 임무다.
 46|
 47|‘그 와중에 오 대 문주 무엇…….’
 48|
 49|역시 열화문이라고 해야 하나?
 50|
 51|일인전승(一人傳承)으로 수백 년간 이어져 내려온 유서 깊은 깡패 문파답다.
 52|
 53|열화문의 역대 문주 중에서는 초야에 묻혀 장수한 이도, 무림에 나가 불꽃처럼 타오르고 단명한 이도 있었지만 늘 천하에서 다섯 손가락 안에 드는 신위를 지닌 괴물들이었다고 들었으니까.
 54|
 55|‘아마 내가 이 자리에 앉을 수 있는 이유 중 하나겠지.’
 56|
 57|무려 이백여 년 전의 일이라고는 해도 남만야수궁과 열화문은 제법 밀접한 관계가 있다.
 58|
 59|K-무림식 해석으로는 단군 할아버지 절친이 세운 문파, 뭐 그쯤 되겠지.
 60|
 61|문제는 내가 사람 패는 데에는 재주가 있어도, 설득하는 것에는 영 재능이 없다는 거다.
 62|
 63|‘그래도 최선을 다해 봐야지.’
 64|
 65|허리를 곧게 편 나는 탁자를 중심으로 자리한 서른두 명의 부족장들을 바라보았다.
 66|
 67|가장 상석에는 야수묘왕. 그의 좌우로는 대족장인 백상과 요희, 흑웅이 차례대로 앉아 있었고 나머지 사람들은 세력 순에 상관없이 자리를 배정받은 듯했다.
 68|
 69|비록 숫자는 적지만, 이들 한 사람 한 사람이 적게는 수백 이상, 많게는 수만의 부족민을 거느린 부족장이라는 것을 생각해 보면 오늘의 이 자리는 남만, 그 자체나 다름없다.
 70|
 71|그리고 내가 그들의 면면을 훑던 그때, 상석에 자리한 야수묘왕이 짧은 침묵을 깨트렸다.
 72|
 73|“자, 그럼.”
 74|
 75|진중한 표정과 위엄 어린 눈빛. 마침내 입을 연 그의 모습에 장내의 공기가 활시위처럼 팽팽하게 당겨진다.
 76|
 77|남만야수궁의 주인다운 카리스마를 흘린 야수묘왕이, 근엄한 목소리로 대회의를 시작을 알리는 역사적인 한 마디를 내뱉었다.
 78|
 79|“다들 식사는 하고 왔나?”
 80|
 81|“……?”
 82|
 83|“요새 안 좋은 일들이 있었지만 그래도 끼니는 거르지 말아야지. 특히 장 족장은 작년에 비해 살이 좀 빠진 것 같은데?”
 84|
 85|“……!”
 86|
 87|역사적이긴 시부럴 거.
 88|
 89|‘내가 지금 뭘 들은 거지.’
 90|
 91|생각지도 못했던 첫 마디에 귀를 의심하고 있던 그때. 조금 전 내게 가장 먼저 포권을 취했던 장 족장이 대답했다.
 92|
 93|“역시 궁주님 눈썰미는 못 속이겠군요. 사실 조금 빠졌습니다.”
 94|
 95|아니. 이걸 받아 준다고?
 96|
 97|“그럴 줄 알았네. 하지만 부족장이라는 사람이 그래서야 쓰나. 부족민들을 생각해서라도 스스로 몸을 보살펴야지. 그런데 자네 나이가 어떻게 되더라?”
 98|
 99|“환갑입니다.”
100|
101|“창창하군. 앞으로 더 먹게.”
102|
103|“존명.”
104|
105|이제는 환청까지 왔는지, 존명이 좆망으로 들린다.
106|
107|‘남만 좆망.’
108|
109|이게 내가 생각했던 부족 대회의가 맞나.
110|
111|나는 아연한 표정으로 서른두 명의 부족장들을 바라봤다.
112|
113|남만 전체를 대표하는 그들은, 야수묘왕의 첫 마디를 신호탄 삼아 듣는 것만으로도 가슴이 조촐해지는 대화를 곳곳에서 주고받는 중이었다.
114|
115|“갈 족장, 소식 들었어. 여섯째가 성인식을 치렀다며?”
116|
117|“일곱째일세.”
118|
119|“내가 헷갈렸군. 자네가 자식을 한둘 낳았어야지. 아무리 기운이 좋아도 열다섯 명이나 낳는 게 말이 되나?”
120|
121|“열일곱 명일세.”
122|
123|“……작년 대회의 때는 분명히 열다섯이었는데?”
124|
125|“둘 더 낳았네. 쌍둥이로.”
126|
127|“아.”
128|
129|한쪽에서는 남만 축구 리그 창설을 노리는 게 아닌가 의심되는 슈퍼 정자맨의 대화가.
130|
131|“구 족장. 얼마 전에 훔쳐 간 가축 돌려놔.”
132|
133|“뭔 놈의 가축?”
134|
135|“목초지에서 감쪽같이 사라진 젖소 쉰두 마리. 자네 부족민들 짓인 거 모를 줄 알았나?”
136|
137|“그런 적 없네.”
138|
139|“네놈이야 당연히 그렇게 말하겠지. 지금 좋게 말할 때 돌려놔.”
140|
141|“아, 진짜! 그런 적 없다니까!”
142|
143|“좋게 말할 때 젖소 내놓으라고! 이 젖소 젖 같은 새끼야!”
144|
145|다른 한쪽에서는 그 많던 젖소는 누가 다 훔쳐 갔을까에 관한 격렬한 고성이.
146|
147|“마치 어제의 기억처럼 떠오르는군. 네놈들이 우리 부족의 영역을 침범하던 그 날이.”
148|
149|“아, 이 인간은 매년 이 지랄이네. 아직 불혹밖에 안 된 주제에 팔십 년 전 일을 왜 자꾸 들먹여?”
150|
151|“나는 선조들의 혼을 물려받았으니까. 그런 의미에서 땅 내놔.”
152|
153|“그게 말이 되나? 선대에서 마무리된 일을 왜 자꾸 끌어오냐고!”
154|
155|“땅 내놔.”
156|
157|“아니 진짜…….”
158|
159|“땅 내놔.”
160|
161|또 다른 구석에서는 환생설을 주장하는 땅귀신의 밀고 당기기가 이어지는 중이다.
162|
163|그리고 이 모든 상황을 황당하게 바라보던 내 귓가에 한 사람의 전음이 파고들었다.
164|
165|- 웃긴 표정이네.
166|
167|나는 슬쩍 고개를 돌려 전음의 주인을 찾았다. 동시에 이쪽을 바라보며 재밌다는 듯 웃고 있는 요희와 눈이 마주쳤다.
168|
169|- 부족 대회의는 늘 이래. 뭐, 남만 곳곳에 흩어져 있다가 일 년에 단 한 번 모이니까 당연하기도 하지만.
170|
171|잠시 고민하던 나는 솔직하게 대답했다.
172|
173|- 그걸 감안해도 너무 개판인데.
174|
175|- 부족 대회의는 남만 전체의 대소사(大小事)를 다루는 자리야. 말 그대로 작은 일 역시 회의 내용에 포함된다는 뜻이지.
176|
177|- ……그 일이 작아도 너무 작은데?
178|
179|- 서른두 개나 되는 부족이 어떻게 화합하며 살아가겠어? 모두가 모인 자리에서 하나씩 결정짓는 거지. 그렇게 앙금을 푸는 거고.
180|
181|콰당!
182|
183|“야, 이 개샛끼야!”
184|
185|“아니, 이 새끼가 미쳤나…….”
186|
187|“네가 그렇게 무공이 강해? 입 닥치고 따라 나와.”
188|
189|젖소에 관해 격론을 벌이다가 마침내 멱살을 움켜잡은 두 족장을 바라본 요희가 덧붙였다.
190|
191|- 물론 예외도 있지.
192|
193|- …….
194|
195|- 금방 정리될 거야. 진짜 대회의는 그때부터가 시작이지.
196|
197|“아. 땅 줘. 땅 달라고.”
198|
199|“허어어. 이 천년지주 같은 새끼.”
200|
201|“그러고 보니까 천 년 전에 우리 조상님들께서…….”
202|
203|“그만! 그마아아안!”
204|
205|금방 정리된다라.
206|
207|음. 아닐 것 같은데.
208|
209|‘진짜 야만인 새끼들인가……?’
210|
211|내가 차마 말하지 못한 진심을 마음속으로 중얼거리던 그때, 요희의 말처럼 혼란스럽던 주위 상황이 하나둘씩 빠르게 정리되더니 새로운 이야기가 흘러나오기 시작했다.
212|
213|“이번 맹수 토벌에서 만족 전사 서른 명이 부상을 입고, 스물둘이 죽었습니다. 근래 들어 유난히 기승을 부리고 있는 듯하니 피해가 더 커지기 전에 내궁에서 나서 주시길 요청하는…….”
214|
215|“갑작스럽게 내린 폭우로 홍수가 발생했습니다. 목초지를 비롯한 인근 가호(家戶) 오십여 채가 물에 잠겼고…….”
216|
217|“황족과 둥족의 분쟁이 종결되었음을 이 자리에서 보고드립니다. 양 측은 합의에 따라 공식 서안을 작성했으며, 향후 십 년간 평화를…….”
218|
219|맹수 토벌에 관한 상황. 재난 재해와 분쟁.
220|
221|전채 요리가 끝나자 슬슬 메인 디쉬가 나오기 시작한다.
222|
223|그리고 그렇게 흘러나오는 이야기들 중에는 제법 신경 써야 할 정보들 역시 포함되어 있었다.
224|
225|“북동쪽에서 괴인(怪人)이 나타났다고 합니다.”
226|
227|괴인?
228|
229|내 의문과 동시에, 지금껏 짧은 대답과 함께 고개만 끄덕이던 야수묘왕이 자세를 바로 세우며 입을 열었다.
230|
231|“괴인이라. 이 이야기는 처음 듣는 듯한데.”
232|
233|“저어. 그것이…….”
234|
235|맨 처음 괴인에 관한 이야기를 꺼낸 부족장이 반신반의하는 표정으로 대답했다.
236|
237|“확실한 정보는 아니라 자신 있게 말씀드릴 수는 없습니다만…….”
238|
239|“정보의 출처가 어딘가?”
240|
241|“사흘 전, 북동쪽의 경계를 넘어온 한족 하나를 붙잡았는데 그자가 알려 주었습니다. 갑작스럽게 나타난 정체 모를 괴인이 귀주(貴州)에서 피바람을 일으키고 있다더군요.”
242|
243|귀주성은 사천, 광서와 함께 남만과 맞닿아 있는 접경지다. 과장 조금 보태자면, 엎어지면 코 닿을 거리라고 해도 과언이 아닐 정도다.
244|
245|‘그런데 귀주에서 괴인이 나타나? 이렇게 갑자기?’
246|
247|찜찜하다. 아니, 찜찜하다 못해 거슬릴 정도다. 그리고 괴인의 정체만큼이나 알 수 없는 낌새를 알아차린 것은 나뿐만이 아니었다.
248|
249|“더 자세히.”
250|
251|눈살을 찌푸린 야수묘왕의 모습에 부족장이 마른침을 꿀꺽 삼켰다.
252|
253|“괴인의 이름도, 나이도 밝혀진 바가 없습니다. 다만 중원의 승려들처럼 민머리에 한 자루 선장(禪杖)을 들고 다니며 지금껏 귀주성에서만 기백 명을 쳐 죽였다고 했는데, 그 때문인지 혈승(血僧)이라는 별호로 불린다고 합니다.”
254|
255|“혈승?”
256|
257|“예. 제가 붙잡은 그 한족도 제법 뛰어난 무림인으로 보였지만, 혈승에 관하여 이야기할 때에는 두려움을 금치 못했습니다.”
258|
259|혈승이라는 살벌한 별호도 그렇지만, 실로 엄청난 무공의 소유자임이 틀림없다.
260|
261|‘귀주도 엄연히 정파의 영역. 무림맹이 손 놓고 있을 리는 없었을 텐데.’
262|
263|그럼에도 불구하고 기백 명을 쳐 죽이며 악명을 떨치다니. 최소 초절정의 무위가 뒷받침되지 않고서야 불가능한 일이다.
264|
265|게다가 놈이 나타난 장소가 하필 남만과 인접한 귀주성이라는 것도 마음에 걸렸다.
266|
267|‘혹시.’
268|
269|기묘한 시기에 갑작스럽게 나타난 정체불명의 괴인. 정파의 영역인 귀주성을 단신으로 휩쓸 만큼의 무위.
270|
271|나로서는 암천과의 연관성을 생각하지 않을 수 없었다. 설령 남천마후와 같은 급의 거물이 아니더라도 가능성은 충분하다.
272|
273|혈주와 서천마군 역시 음양쌍귀(陰陽雙鬼)나 기련삼괴(祁連三怪)와 같은 초절정 고수들을 휘하에 두었으니까.
274|
275|‘그리고 그 혈승이라는 놈의 목적이 남만이라면……?’
276|
277|거기까지 생각이 다다른 내가 부족장을 향해 처음으로 입을 뗐다.
278|
279|“그 혈승이라는 자가 어디로 향하는지 알 수 있습니까?”
280|

I was still doubting my ears when Chief Jang—the first to offer me a cupped-fist salute earlier—answered.

[P28]
“As expected, nothing gets past the Palace Lord’s keen eyes. I have lost a little weight.”

[P29]
*No. He’s actually going along with this?*

[P30]
“I thought so. But a chieftain can’t neglect his health. You have to take care of yourself for your tribespeople’s sake. How old are you again?”

[P31]
“Sixty.”

[P32]
“You’re still in the prime of life. Eat more.”

[P33]
“Jonmyeong.”[^2]

[P34]
Now I was hearing things, too. *Jonmyeong* sounded like *jonmang*—“fucked.”

[P35]
*Nanman is fucked.*

[P36]
Was this really the Tribal Grand Council I’d imagined?

[P37]
I stared at the thirty-two chieftains in disbelief.

[P38]
These people represented all of Nanman. Yet the Beast Miao King’s opening words had apparently been their cue to start conversations all over the hall that made my spirit shrink just listening to them.

[P39]
“Chief Gal, I heard your sixth child had their coming-of-age ceremony.”

[P40]
“My seventh.”

[P41]
“I got them mixed up. If only you’d stopped at one or two. I don’t care how vigorous you are—fifteen children?”

[P42]
“Seventeen.”

[P43]
“…You definitely had fifteen at last year’s council.”

[P44]
“We had two more. Twins.”

[P45]
“Oh.”

[P46]
On one side, a super-sperm man seemed to be working toward founding a Nanman soccer league.

[P47]
“Chief Gu. Return the livestock you stole.”

[P48]
“What livestock?”

[P49]
“The fifty-two dairy cows that vanished from the pasture. You think I don’t know your tribespeople took them?”

[P50]
“They didn’t.”

[P51]
“Of course you’d say that. Return them while I’m asking nicely.”

[P52]
“Oh, come on! I’m telling you, we didn’t take them!”

[P53]
“I said hand over the cows while I’m asking nicely, you cow-udder bastard!”

[P54]
On another, a furious argument raged over who had stolen all those cows.

[P55]
“I remember it as if it were yesterday. The day you bastards trespassed on our tribe’s land.”

[P56]
“Oh, this again? Every damn year. You’re barely forty. Why do you keep bringing up something that happened eighty years ago?”

[P57]
“Because I inherited the spirits of my ancestors. So give me the land.”

[P58]
“How does that make sense? Our predecessors settled this!”

[P59]
“Give me the land.”

[P60]
“No, seriously…”

[P61]
“Give me the land.”

[P62]
Elsewhere, a land-obsessed ghost claiming reincarnation kept up his back-and-forth.

[P63]
As I watched it all in disbelief, someone’s Sound Transmission reached my ear.

[P64]
—That’s a funny expression.

[P65]
I turned my head slightly and met Yohi’s eyes. She was watching me with an amused smile.

[P66]
—The Tribal Grand Council is always like this. Everyone’s scattered across Nanman and only gets together once a year, so I suppose it’s natural.

[P67]
I thought for a moment, then answered honestly.

[P68]
—Even so, this is a complete shitshow.

[P69]
—The Tribal Grand Council handles all of Nanman’s affairs, major and minor. *Minor* means the small ones come up, too.

[P70]
—…These are a little *too* minor.

[P71]
—How else are thirty-two tribes supposed to live together in harmony? They settle things one by one when everyone’s gathered. It lets them clear up old grudges.

[P72]
*Crash!*

[P73]
“You son of a bitch!”

[P74]
“Is this bastard out of his mind…?”

[P75]
“You think your martial arts are that strong? Shut up and come outside.”

[P76]
The two chieftains arguing over the cows had finally grabbed each other by the collars. Yohi looked at them and added:

[P77]
—Of course, there are exceptions.

[P78]
—…

[P79]
—They’ll settle down soon. That’s when the real council starts.

[P80]
“Ah, give me the land. I said give it to me.”

[P81]
“Oh, you Thousand-Year Spider bastard.”

[P82]
“Come to think of it, a thousand years ago, our ancestors…”

[P83]
“Stop! Stoooop!”

[P84]
*They’ll settle down soon,* she said.

[P85]
Hmm. I had my doubts.

[P86]
*Are these people really just a bunch of barbarians…?*

[P87]
I kept that thought to myself. But just as Yohi had said, the chaos began to subside, one dispute at a time, and new matters came up.

[P88]
“Thirty Man warriors were wounded and twenty-two killed in this latest ferocious-beast hunt. The beasts have been especially active lately, so we ask the Inner Palace to intervene before the losses grow…”

[P89]
“Sudden heavy rain caused flooding. The pastures and some fifty nearby homes were submerged…”

[P90]
“I report that the dispute between the Huang and Dong tribes has been resolved. Both sides have drawn up an official written agreement and will maintain peace for the next ten years…”

[P91]
Ferocious-beast hunts. Floods. Tribal disputes.

[P92]
The appetizers were over. Now the main dishes were coming out.

[P93]
And among those reports was something that deserved serious attention.

[P94]
“They say a strange man has appeared in the northeast.”

[P95]
*A strange man?*

[P96]
The Beast Miao King, who had only given short answers and nodded until now, sat up straight.

[P97]
“A strange man? This is the first I’ve heard of it.”

[P98]
“W-well…”

[P99]
The chieftain who had raised the matter looked uncertain.

[P100]
“The information hasn’t been confirmed, so I can’t speak with confidence…”

[P101]
“Where did it come from?”

[P102]
“Three days ago, we captured a Han Chinese man who crossed the northeastern border. He told us an unidentified man had appeared out of nowhere and was leaving a trail of blood through Guizhou.”

[P103]
Guizhou bordered Nanman, as did Sichuan and Guangxi. Exaggerating only a little, it was close enough to trip and land there.

[P104]
*But some strange man suddenly appeared in Guizhou?*

[P105]
Something felt off. More than off—it nagged at me. And I wasn’t the only one who sensed there was more to this than the stranger’s unknown identity.

[P106]
“Tell me more.”

[P107]
The chieftain swallowed at the sight of the Beast Miao King’s frown.

[P108]
“Neither his name nor his age is known. They say he’s bald like a monk from the Central Plains and carries a Zen staff. He’s beaten several hundred people to death in Guizhou alone. That’s apparently why they call him the Blood Monk.”

[P109]
“The Blood Monk?”

[P110]
“Yes. The Han Chinese man we captured seemed to be a fairly skilled martial artist himself, but he couldn’t hide his fear when he spoke of him.”

[P111]
The sobriquet was grim enough. Its owner had to possess astonishing martial arts.

[P112]
*Guizhou is orthodox faction territory. The Murim Alliance wouldn’t have just stood by.*

[P113]
Yet the Blood Monk had killed several hundred people and made a name for himself. Without at least Supreme Peak-level martial prowess, that would have been impossible.

[P114]
It also bothered me that he’d appeared in Guizhou, right beside Nanman.

[P115]
*Could it be…?*

[P116]
An unidentified man appearing at such a strange time. Strong enough to rampage alone through Guizhou, a stronghold of the orthodox faction.

[P117]
I couldn’t help thinking of Dark Heaven. He might not be a major figure on the Southern Heaven Demon Empress’s level, but the possibility was there. The Blood Lord and the Western Heaven Demon Lord had commanded Supreme Peak masters like the Yin-Yang Twin Ghosts and the Qilian Three Fiends.

[P118]
*And what if the Blood Monk is headed for Nanman?*

[P119]
For the first time, I spoke to the chieftain.

[P120]
“Do you know where the Blood Monk is going?”

[P121]
“I wanted to ask him myself, but there’s no way to know now.”

[P122]
“What do you mean?”

[P123]
The chieftain shook his head with a faint sigh.

[P124]
“The man died.”

[P125]
“What?”

[P126]
“He died before I could ask anything else. He was badly injured to begin with, and I don’t think he adapted to the sudden change in environment. Then the heavy rain brought a flood, and we couldn’t take proper measures.”

[P127]
“…!”

[P128]
The Blood Monk’s appearance. And the death of our only witness.

[P129]
Silence settled over the hall. Then someone who had said nothing since the council began spoke up.

[P130]
“Injury, endemic disease, and death. They happen often enough.”

[P131]
Everyone turned toward the voice.

[P132]
Baeksang.

[P133]
“The Slaughter Saint appearing in the Central Plains is no different. Han Chinese have always been that way. Though they are one people, they’ve kept their world going by killing one another. In short…”

[P134]
His tone and expression remained perfectly calm. His voice was cold.

[P135]
“There’s no reason for Nanman to concern itself with affairs in the Central Plains. None at all.”

[P136]
Maybe I was reading too much into it. But something about that struck me as strange.

[P137]
Baeksang led the Bai people, with Nanman’s second-largest population and sphere of influence. Yet he wanted to ignore something happening right next door.

[P138]
I watched him for a moment, then spoke.

[P139]
“What if the Blood Monk is heading south?”

[P140]
The chieftains who grasped my meaning widened their eyes. Baeksang answered without a trace of hesitation.

[P141]
“Nanman isn’t the only place bordering Guizhou. Beyond Guangxi lies the open sea. With a favorable wind, one can sail to Hainan in ten days.”

[P142]
“So you think it’s unlikely the Blood Monk will enter Nanman?”

[P143]
“Why would he come all the way here? Rather than face venomous beasts, ferocious beasts, and countless Nanman warriors, he could go through Guangxi to the sea…”

[P144]
“There is a reason. One clear reason. But…”

[P145]
I cut him off firmly and held his gaze.

[P146]
“Strangely enough, you seem to be the only one who doesn’t know it.”

[P147]
“What?”

[P148]
“Or did you agree with someone to pretend you didn’t know from the start?”

[P149]
At that moment—

[P150]
*Fwoosh. Whoomph.*

[P151]
The wavering torches went out.

[P152]
In the darkness that fell over the vast hall, a pair of eyes radiated a piercing chill.

[P153]
“You have finally crossed the line.”

[P154]
*Whoosh!*

[P155]
“Well.”

[P156]
An immense wave of qi bore down on me from every direction, squeezing my entire body. I spoke calmly.

[P157]
“I think you’re the one crossing it.”

[P158]
[^1]: Dangun is the legendary founder of Korea’s first kingdom; “Grandfather Dangun” jokingly invokes a distant shared ancestor.
[^2]: *Jonmyeong* means “As you command.” It differs by one vowel from *jonmang*, crude slang for being utterly ruined.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). ## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.

- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Output contract

Return exactly one JSON object and no Markdown fence or prose:

Reasons must name the veto, or say that SOL keeps sense and voice. Do not merely say one version is "better" or "more natural" without stating what changed.

Keep reasons brief. Do not adjudicate unchanged passages. Do not call tools.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

[P8]

[P9]

[P12]
By K-Murim logic, it was basically a sect founded by Grandfather Dangun’s best friend.[^1]

[P14]
The problem was that while I had a talent for beating people up, I had absolutely no talent for persuasion.

[P15]
*Still, I have to do my best.*

[P16]
I straightened my back and looked at the thirty-two chieftains seated around the table.

[P17]
The Beast Miao King occupied the highest seat. To his left and right sat the great chieftains Baeksang, Yohi, and Heugung, in that order, while the others appeared to have been assigned their seats without regard to the strength of their factions.

[P18]
There might not have been many of them, but each and every one was a chieftain commanding anywhere from several hundred to tens of thousands of tribespeople.

[P19]
When I considered that, this gathering was practically Nanman itself.

[P20]
And just as I was studying their faces, the Beast Miao King, seated at the head of the table, broke the brief silence.

[P21]
“Well, then.”

[P22]
His expression was solemn, and his gaze was filled with dignity. At last, he opened his mouth, and the air in the room drew taut like a bowstring.

[P23]
The Beast Miao King radiated the charisma befitting the master of the Nanman Beast Palace and uttered a historic first sentence in a grave voice.

[P24]
“Did everyone eat before coming here?”

[P25]
“……?”

[P26]
“We’ve had some unpleasant things happen lately, but you still shouldn’t skip your meals. In particular, Chief Jang, you seem to have lost a little weight compared to last year.”

[P27]
“……!”

[P28]
*Historic, my ass.*

[P29]
*What did I just hear?*

[P30]
While I was still doubting my ears at that completely unexpected opening, Chief Jang—the first person to offer me a cupped-fist salute earlier—answered.

[P31]
“As expected, nothing gets past the Palace Lord’s keen eyes. I have lost a little weight, in fact.”

[P32]
*No. He’s actually going along with this?*

[P33]
“I thought so. But a man who calls himself a chieftain cannot be neglecting himself like that. You should take care of your health for the sake of your tribespeople. Now, how old are you again?”

[P34]
“I am sixty.”

[P35]
“You’re still in the prime of life. Eat more from now on.”

[P36]
“Jonmyeong.”[^2]

[P37]
Now I was hearing things too, because *jonmyeong* sounded like *jonmang*—“fucked.”

[P38]
*Nanman is fucked.*

[P39]

[P40]

[P41]
Representing all of Nanman, they had taken the Beast Miao King’s first words as a starting signal and were now exchanging conversations in various corners that made my heart feel cramped just listening to them.

[P42]
“Chief Gal, I heard the news. Your sixth child had their coming-of-age ceremony?”

[P43]
“My seventh.”

[P44]
“I got confused. If only you’d stopped at one or two. No matter how vigorous you are, how can you have fifteen?”

[P45]
“Seventeen.”

[P46]
“……At last year’s grand council, you definitely had fifteen.”

[P47]
“I had two more. Twins.”

[P48]
“Oh.”

[P49]
On one side was a conversation with a super-sperm man who seemed intent on founding a Nanman soccer league.

[P50]
“Chief Gu. Return the livestock you stole a while ago.”

[P51]
“What livestock?”

[P52]
“The fifty-two dairy cows that vanished from the pasture without a trace. Did you think I wouldn’t know your tribespeople did it?”

[P53]
“I have never done such a thing.”

[P54]
“Of course you’d say that. Return them while I’m still asking nicely.”

[P55]
“Oh, for real! I said I never did that!”

[P56]
“I said hand over the cows while I’m asking nicely! You cow-udder bastard!”

[P57]
On the other side, a furious argument raged over the question of who had stolen all those cows.

[P58]
“It comes back to me as clearly as yesterday—the day you bastards trespassed into our tribal territory.”

[P59]
“Damn it, this guy does this every year. You’re barely forty, so why do you keep bringing up something that happened eighty years ago?”

[P60]
“I inherited the spirits of my ancestors. In that sense, hand over the land.”

[P61]
“How does that make any sense? Why do you keep dragging up something that was settled by the previous generation?”

[P62]
“Hand over the land.”

[P63]
“No, seriously……”

[P64]
“Hand over the land.”

[P65]

[P66]

[P67]
—You have a funny expression.

[P68]

[P69]

[P70]

[P71]

[P72]

[P73]

[P75]

[P76]
“You goddamn mutt!”

[P77]
“Has this bastard lost his mind……?”

[P78]
“You think your martial arts are that strong? Shut your mouth and come outside.”

[P80]

[P81]
—……

[P82]

[P84]
“Gaaah. You Thousand-Year Spider bastard.”

[P85]
“Come to think of it, a thousand years ago, our ancestors……”

[P86]
“Stop! Stoooop!”

[P87]

[P88]

[P89]

[P91]

[P92]
“Sudden torrential rain caused a flood. The pasture and around fifty nearby homes were submerged……”

[P93]
“I hereby report that the dispute between the Huang and Dong tribes has come to an end. In accordance with the agreement, both sides have drawn up an official document, and peace will be maintained for the next ten years……”

[P94]
The situation surrounding the ferocious-beast hunt. Natural disasters and disputes.

[P95]
Once the appetizers were finished, the main dishes began to arrive.

[P97]
“They say a strange figure has appeared in the northeast.”

[P100]
“A strange figure. This is the first I have heard of it.”

[P101]
“W-well, the thing is……”

[P102]

[P103]
“I cannot speak with confidence because the information has not been confirmed……”

[P104]
“Where did the information come from?”

[P105]
“Three days ago, we captured a Han Chinese man who had crossed the northeastern border. He told us about it. Apparently, an unidentified strange man appeared out of nowhere and is stirring up a bloodbath in Guizhou.”

[P106]

[P107]
*But a strange man appeared in Guizhou? So suddenly?*

[P108]

[P109]

[P110]
“More details.”

[P111]

[P112]

[P113]
“Blood Monk?”

[P114]
“Yes. The Han Chinese man we captured appeared to be a fairly skilled martial artist himself, but he could not hide his fear whenever he spoke about the Blood Monk.”

[P115]

[P116]
*Guizhou is unquestionably orthodox faction territory. The Murim Alliance couldn’t possibly have just stood by and done nothing.*

[P117]
And yet the man had killed several hundred people and earned a notorious reputation. It would have been impossible without at least Supreme Peak-level martial prowess.

[P118]
Besides, it bothered me that he had appeared in Guizhou—a region directly adjacent to Nanman.

[P119]
*Could it be……?*

[P120]
An unidentified strange man who had appeared out of nowhere at an unusual time. Martial prowess powerful enough to sweep through Guizhou, a land of the orthodox faction, single-handedly.

[P121]

[P122]
The Blood Lord and the Western Heaven Demon Lord had also kept Supreme Peak masters such as the Yin-Yang Twin Ghosts and the Qilian Three Fiends under their command.

[P123]
*And what if the Blood Monk’s target is Nanman……?*

[P124]

[P125]
“Is it possible to know where the Blood Monk is headed?”

[P126]
“I would have liked to ask him myself, but there is no way to know now.”

[P127]
“What do you mean……”

[P128]
The chieftain shook his head with a faint sigh and answered.

[P129]
“He is dead.”

[P130]
“What?”

[P131]
“He died before I could ask him anything else. He was already suffering from serious injuries, to begin with, and it seems he was unable to adapt to the sudden change in environment. A torrential rain came down at just the wrong time and caused a flood, so we could not take proper measures.”

[P132]
“……!”

[P133]
The Blood Monk’s appearance.

[P134]
And now, the death of the only witness we had.

[P135]
As silence descended over the room, someone who had remained silent since the grand council began abruptly spoke.

[P136]
“Injury, endemic disease, and death. Such things happen from time to time.”

[P137]
At the sudden voice, everyone’s gaze turned toward the same place.

[P138]
Baeksang.

[P139]
It was him.

[P140]
“The Slaughter Saint appearing in the Central Plains is no different. Han Chinese have always been that way. Despite being one people, they have maintained the present world by killing and being killed among themselves. In short……”

[P141]

[P142]

[P143]

[P144]

[P145]

[P146]

[P150]

[P151]
“What reason would he have to come all the way here? Rather than face venomous beasts, ferocious beasts, and countless Nanman warriors, he could simply head to the sea through Guangxi……”

[P152]
“There is one reason. A single, unmistakable reason. But……”

[P153]
I forcefully cut him off before he could continue, fixing Baeksang with a grave, steady gaze as I went on.

[P154]
“Strangely enough, you seem to be the only one who doesn’t know that.”

[P155]
“What?”

[P156]
“Or……”

[P157]
I paused before continuing.

[P158]
“Did you make some kind of agreement with someone to pretend from the very beginning that you didn’t know?”

[P159]
At that moment—

[P160]
*Fwoosh. Whoomph.*

[P161]
The wavering torchlight went out.

[P162]

[P163]
“You have finally crossed the line.”

[P164]
*Whoosh!*

[P165]
“Well.”

[P166]
I felt the enormous martial aura squeezing my entire body from every direction and muttered calmly.

[P167]
“It seems you’re the one crossing the line.”

*And what if the Blood Monk is headed for Nanman?*

[P119]
For the first time, I spoke to the chieftain.

[P120]
“Do you know where the Blood Monk is going?”

[P121]
“I wanted to ask him myself, but there’s no way to know now.”

[P122]
“What do you mean?”

[P123]
The chieftain shook his head with a faint sigh.

[P124]
“The man died.”

[P125]
“What?”

[P126]
“He died before I could ask anything else. He was badly injured to begin with, and I don’t think he adapted to the sudden change in environment. Then the heavy rain brought a flood, and we couldn’t take proper measures.”

[P127]
“…!”

[P128]
The Blood Monk’s appearance. And the death of our only witness.

[P129]
Silence settled over the hall. Then someone who had said nothing since the council began spoke up.

[P130]
“Injury, endemic disease, and death. They happen often enough.”

[P131]
Everyone turned toward the voice.

[P132]
Baeksang.

[P133]
“The Slaughter Saint appearing in the Central Plains is no different. Han Chinese have always been that way. Though they are one people, they’ve kept their world going by killing one another. In short…”

[P134]
His tone and expression remained perfectly calm. His voice was cold.

[P135]
“There’s no reason for Nanman to concern itself with affairs in the Central Plains. None at all.”

[P136]
Maybe I was reading too much into it. But something about that struck me as strange.

[P137]
Baeksang led the Bai people, with Nanman’s second-largest population and sphere of influence. Yet he wanted to ignore something happening right next door.

[P138]
I watched him for a moment, then spoke.

[P139]
“What if the Blood Monk is heading south?”

[P140]
The chieftains who grasped my meaning widened their eyes. Baeksang answered without a trace of hesitation.

[P141]
“Nanman isn’t the only place bordering Guizhou. Beyond Guangxi lies the open sea. With a favorable wind, one can sail to Hainan in ten days.”

[P142]
“So you think it’s unlikely the Blood Monk will enter Nanman?”

[P143]
“Why would he come all the way here? Rather than face venomous beasts, ferocious beasts, and countless Nanman warriors, he could go through Guangxi to the sea…”

[P144]
“There is a reason. One clear reason. But…”

[P145]
I cut him off firmly and held his gaze.

[P146]
“Strangely enough, you seem to be the only one who doesn’t know it.”

[P147]
“What?”

[P148]
“Or did you agree with someone to pretend you didn’t know from the start?”

[P149]
At that moment—

[P150]
*Fwoosh. Whoomph.*

[P151]
The wavering torches went out.

[P152]
In the darkness that fell over the vast hall, a pair of eyes radiated a piercing chill.

[P153]
“You have finally crossed the line.”

[P154]
*Whoosh!*

[P155]
“Well.”

[P156]
An immense wave of qi bore down on me from every direction, squeezing my entire body. I spoke calmly.

[P157]
“I think you’re the one crossing it.”

[^2]: *Jonmyeong* means “As you command.” It differs by one vowel from *jonmang*, crude slang for being utterly ruined.

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
